title: Slate job
description: One long-running job in the machine-wide queue (DATA/jobs/<id>.json). Written only by slate.jobs; read it with `slate job status <id> --json`.

kind.description: What the job is (render, master, whisper, tts, music, generation, bank, ...).

argv.description: The command, as an argv list (never a shell string). A leading 'slate' runs this checkout's CLI.

run_argv.description: What actually ran: caffeinate -i, nice, then argv.

disk_path.description: The folder whose volume the job writes to (disk checks).

launch.description: Token of the current launch, so a stale supervisor never writes.

pid.description: The job's supervisor (also its process-group leader).

proc_start.description: The supervisor's start time, so a reused pid isn't mistaken for it.

cmd_pid.description: The command the supervisor runs. It leads its own process group (slate.procs gives every child one), so a dead supervisor's command can still be found and stopped.

cmd_start.description: The command's start time, checked before it's signalled.

not_before.description: A requeued job waits until then (backoff after a busy or temporary failure).

try_later.description: Written by the job's own command as it exits 75 (try later): the vendor's Retry-After and why. Read and cleared when the job goes back in the queue, so its backoff is never shorter than the vendor asked.

retries.description: Times a person or agent sent it back with `slate job retry`.

resumable.description: The command resumes by frame, line or act, so running it again after a crash is safe.

reason.description: Why the job is in its state (failed, requeued, cancelled, stopped).

waiting.description: Why a queued job hasn't started yet.

holds.description: Slots the supervisor holds right now.

env.description: Slate settings captured at submit (folders, replay mode). Never keys: those come from the Keychain.

context.description: The agent that submitted it (claude-code, codex, openclaw), or null for a person.

live.description: True when the job may spend (submitted with --live or outside replay mode).
